cases.user_message: Делаем автоклассификацию обращений в поддержку банка через LLM. Категорий 42 (от «блокировка карты» и «не пришёл перевод СБП» до «вопрос по налоговому вычету по ИИС» и «спор по chargeback»). Сейчас в системном промпте список категорий с описаниями и 8 примеров размеченных обращений, одни и те же для всех запросов. На частых категориях точность около 90%, а на редких (их штук 15, в сумме ~12% трафика) падает до 50-55%: ИИС путают с вкладами, chargeback с «ошибочным переводом». Размеченных обращений у нас около 6 000, по каждой категории минимум 40. Коллега предлагает просто запихнуть в промпт по 3 примера на каждую категорию, это ~126 примеров, но выходит около 20k токенов на каждый запрос при потоке 30 тысяч обращений в день. Либо можно вместо этого переподобрать наши 8 примеров, сделать их «потруднее», чтобы покрывали редкие категории. Какой вариант лучше и как выбрать примеры?
cases.why_in_scope: The implant pushes toward choosing, per incoming ticket, a small set (2-5) of the most similar labeled examples from the existing 6 000-ticket pool via embedding/keyword search, placing the most similar closest to the ticket. A strong model without it may stay within the static framing: tweak the fixed 8 examples, rewrite category descriptions, accept the colleague's 126-example prompt, or jump to fine-tuning, missing that the labeled set can serve as a retrieval pool that fixes rare-category confusion without the token cost.
rubric: Recommends selecting examples per ticket from the existing labeled set by similarity (e.g. embeddings or keyword search) instead of a fixed set or all 126 examples in every prompt
Gives a concrete small number of retrieved examples per request (roughly 2-10) and/or advises placing the most similar example closest to the ticket being classified
Addresses the colleague's proposal with the cost/context trade-off (about 20k tokens x 30 000 requests/day) rather than ignoring it
Mentions at least one practical caveat or check: quality of the labeled pool, retrieval latency, or measuring per-category accuracy on a held-out set for the rare categories

cases.user_message: We run an intent router for a travel app chatbot on gpt-4o-mini. 27 intents (change_booking, cancel_booking, refund_status, baggage_allowance, seat_selection, visa_question, etc.). The prompt lists the intents with one-line descriptions plus 10 hand-picked English example utterances with their labels, same for every call. Traffic is ~40% English, 35% German, 25% Spanish. Overall accuracy on our 1,500-utterance labeled eval set is 84%, but German and Spanish users asking about refunds get routed to cancel_booking a lot, and seat_selection vs. change_booking gets mixed up in all languages. We also have ~9,000 labeled production utterances in all three languages sitting in a spreadsheet. I've already tried rewriting the intent descriptions twice and it barely moved. My plan is to translate the 10 examples into German and Spanish and hand-pick maybe 20 more that cover the confused pairs, so ~50 fixed examples total. Is that the right move, and which examples should I pick?
cases.why_in_scope: Following the implant, the answer should turn the 9,000 labeled multilingual utterances into a pool and retrieve the few most similar ones (ideally same language and near the confused intents) for each incoming message, ordered with the closest example last, instead of a static English-only set. Without it, a strong model may keep suggesting more description tweaks, adding a few static German/Spanish examples, or fine-tuning, and overlook per-query example selection from the data the user already has.
rubric: Recommends retrieving a small number of the most similar labeled utterances per incoming message from the ~9,000-utterance set (e.g. via multilingual embeddings) rather than using the same 10 examples for every call
Addresses the language mismatch explicitly, e.g. retrieved examples should match or be close to the user's language (German/Spanish), not only English

Tackles the specific confusions (refund_status vs cancel_booking, seat_selection vs change_booking), e.g. ensuring contrasting examples of both intents can appear, or placing the most similar example closest to the query
Advises validating the change against the existing 1,500-utterance eval set, ideally broken down per language and per intent

checker_notes: Both cases were too easy to answer with retrieval-based example selection without help, so each user message now ends with a static-example plan (re-pick 8 'harder' examples; translate plus ~50 hand-picked fixed examples) that pulls the answer back toward a fixed set, without leaking the technique. Case 2's last rubric item had two requirements (per-language eval and keeping eval data out of the pool); it now checks only the per-language eval. Agent prompt_engineer kept because the component has no owners.
